evals.prompt: Create an Excalidraw architecture diagram for a social-media platform backend: web clients and mobile clients connect through a load balancer to an API gateway. Behind the gateway are a Feed service, a Users service, a Media service, and a Messaging service. Feed reads from a Feed DB and a Redis cache. Users reads from a Users DB. Media stores to S3-compatible object storage. Messaging uses a Postgres DB and a Kafka topic for fan-out. Save to /tmp/eval-arch.excalidraw.
evals.expected_output: A valid .excalidraw file with all named components arranged in a layered architecture with orthogonal arrow routing and no overlaps.
expectations: Output file /tmp/eval-arch.excalidraw is valid Excalidraw JSON with type 'excalidraw' and version 2
Diagram contains all named components as rectangle elements with bound text labels
Every connection is represented by an arrow with startBinding and endBinding set to real element IDs
No two shape elements overlap
At most 4 distinct fill colours
All text elements use fontFamily 2 or 3
All elements have roughness 0
All text fits within its container (no truncation)

rubric.correctness: All named components present; all stated connections exist with correct direction
rubric.layout: No overlapping elements; no arrow crossings; components visually grouped by tier or function
rubric.labels: Every label fully readable; no truncation; no collisions
rubric.shapes: Services/datastores/queues/external kinds visibly distinct by colour
rubric.typography: Helvetica; labels inside shapes; font size >= 14px
rubric.colour: <=4 accent colours; stroke darker than fill; semantic colour per kind

evals.prompt: Create an Excalidraw diagram for a password-reset flow with these actors: User, Web App, API, Auth Service, Email Provider. User enters email in Web App, Web App POSTs to API, API asks Auth Service to generate a reset token, Auth Service stores the token and asks Email Provider to send a link, Email Provider returns success, User clicks the link, Web App shows reset form, user submits new password, API asks Auth Service to verify token and update password, Auth returns OK. Save to /tmp/eval-sequence.excalidraw.
evals.expected_output: A valid .excalidraw file showing the password-reset flow with all 5 actors and the complete message sequence, using orthogonal arrows.
expectations: Output file /tmp/eval-sequence.excalidraw is valid Excalidraw JSON
Diagram contains nodes for all 5 actors: User, Web App, API, Auth Service, Email Provider
All message edges are present covering the full request-response flow
Every arrow has startBinding and endBinding to real element IDs
All text fits within its container
All elements have roughness 0

rubric.correctness: All 5 actors present; all messages in correct order; request and response arcs present
rubric.layout: Clean orthogonal routing; no arrow crossings; actors clearly separated
rubric.labels: Every message labelled and fully readable; requests vs responses distinguishable

evals.prompt: Create an Excalidraw flowchart for a PR review process: developer opens PR, CI runs tests, if tests fail developer fixes and re-pushes, if tests pass a reviewer is auto-assigned, reviewer approves or requests changes, if changes requested developer addresses and re-pushes (back to CI), if approved the PR is merged to main, triggering a deploy pipeline. Save to /tmp/eval-flow.excalidraw.
evals.expected_output: A valid .excalidraw file showing the PR review flowchart with process steps, decision points, and feedback loops, using orthogonal arrows.
expectations: Output file /tmp/eval-flow.excalidraw is valid Excalidraw JSON
Diagram contains decision nodes (kind: decision) for test pass/fail and review approve/reject
Diagram contains a feedback loop from changes-requested back to CI
Diagram ends with merge and deploy steps
Every arrow has startBinding and endBinding to real element IDs
All text fits within its container
All elements have roughness 0

rubric.correctness: All named steps present; decision points correctly branching; feedback loops back to CI
rubric.layout: Top-to-bottom flow; clean orthogonal routing; decision branches clearly separated; loops readable
rubric.labels: Decision branches labelled; all text fully readable; no truncation
rubric.shapes: Rectangles for processes, diamonds/different colour for decisions
rubric.colour: Semantic colour for decision vs process vs terminal
